verdict: McDonald's grew operating profit 7% to $3.6B on just 1% revenue growth — franchise fees and cost discipline did the lifting while U.S. guest counts slipped slightly.

segments.name: Franchised restaurants
segments.note: Rent and royalty fees paid by franchisees — the profit engine. McDonald's owns many restaurant sites and leases them to the operators who run them.

segments.name: Company-owned restaurants
segments.note: Food sales at restaurants McDonald's runs itself — a shrinking share, as more stores are sold to franchisees.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Fees from developmental licensees and affiliates abroad, plus other services.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Head office, marketing support and running the global franchising machine — includes $118M of depreciation and amortization.

takeaways.title: Comps grew — barely, at home
takeaways.text: Global comparable sales rose 1.5%, but U.S. comps slipped 0.2% as guest counts fell; international licensed markets led with +4.2%.

takeaways.title: The system dwarfs the P&L
takeaways.text: Systemwide sales topped $38B, up 4% — McDonald's books only the fees on most of it. Loyalty members alone spent more than $11B in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Profit per share outran sales
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose 10% to $3.51 on cost cuts and a shrinking share count, and the quarterly dividend was raised 4% to $1.93 per share.

otherDetail: Other expense of $407M, net — $408M of interest expense on McDonald's borrowings, partly offset by $1M of nonoperating income.
footerNote: McDonald's own revenue is mostly fees: franchisees rung up over $38B of systemwide sales in the quarter, of which McDonald's records only its rent, royalties and company-restaurant sales.
oneTimers: Results include $56M of pre-tax restructuring charges from the 'Accelerating the Organization' program (about $0.06 per share). Excluding them, EPS was $3.57.
